candidates.name: Museo Diocesano
candidates.price: €7; combined ticked incl. museum, Terme Achilliane, Benedictine Monastery €13
candidates.content: The collection of the museum contains various religious artefacts from the Cathedral and some other churches around. Its ticket office also sells tickets to the Terme Achilliane.

candidates.name: Castello Ursino
candidates.content: It was built in the 13th century as a royal castle of the Kingdom of Sicily, and ilater became the seat of the Sicilian Parliament. It hosts the Museo Civico (civic museum), which displays Greek and Roman artifacts from the city;

candidates.name: Terme Achilliane
candidates.content: The remains of a small part of a large ancient baths located underground is open for the public. It's under the Catania's Cathedral square. Some parts of mosaics and marble floor as well as some remains of decorated walls. The rem

candidates.name: Chiesa di San Nicolò l'Arena
candidates.price: Free entrance; visit to the eaves €3
candidates.content: It is an unachieved church which was supposed to be the biggest one in Sicily.

candidates.name: Chiesa di San Francesco Borgia
candidates.content: Today the church used for various cultural events. Next to the church is a former Jesuit college.

candidates.name: Palazzo Gravina-Cruyllas
candidates.content: It is the birthplace of Vincenzo Bellini. Thete are two museums here.

candidates.name: Quattro Canti
candidates.content: A square at the intersection of Via Etnea with Via di Sangiuliano. It is somewhat reminiscent to the other octagonal squares in Italy: Quattro Canti at the piazza Vigliena in Palermo, Quattro Canti in Paternò, and Quattro Fontane

candidates.name: Castello di Aci
candidates.content: A medieval castle perched on a giant rock, right over the sea. Contains a small civic museum.

candidates.name: Cattedrale di Sant'Agata
candidates.content: An imposing cathedral, well worth visiting. Also see for Terme Achilliane and Museo Diocesano which are located there.

candidates.name: Monastero dei Benedettini di San Nicolò l'Arena
candidates.price: Free entrance to the exterior areas, interor with guided tour €10, which starts daily around 13:00 and hourly during summer. English tours at 13:00 and 16:00
candidates.content: It is the oldest one in Sicily and it is one of the biggest monasteries in Europe. It hosts now the Faculty of Literature of the University of Catania.

candidates.name: Via Crociferi
candidates.content: It's a centre of an ecclesiastical architecture in Catania: in no more than 200 m there are 4 churches, 3 monasteries and a college.

candidates.name: Palazzo Biscari
candidates.content: It is one of the most interesting baroque palaces in Catania. The palace is privately owned. Check with the tourist office to arrange a visit.

candidates.name: Piazza del Duomo
candidates.content: An attractive, lively baroque square. Here you can find the Fontana dell'Elefante (Elephant Fountain) or U Liotru - the symbol of the city. There are three buildings here that are World Heritage Sites. The square is also an entran

candidates.name: Chiesa della Badia di Sant'Agata
candidates.hours: Guided tours to the dome and the terraces: Tue 09:00-12:00, Wed-Sat 09:30 -12:30, 15:30-17:30; Sun 09:30-12:30, 19:00-20:30

candidates.name: Monastero di San Benedetto
candidates.content: A splendid baroque monument.

candidates.name: Terme della Rotonda
candidates.content: The remains of ancient Roman baths.

candidates.name: Anfiteatro Romano
candidates.content: Some modest remains amidst the square.

candidates.name: Teatro Massimo Bellini
candidates.content: A 19th-century opera theatre named after the Catania-born composer Vincenzo Bellini. The square before the theatre is a popular meeting place among the local young people, so its neighbourhood is very lively and busy by night.

candidates.name: Palazzo Della Cultura
candidates.alt: ex Convento S.Placido, aka Palazzo Platamone
candidates.content: A former monastery, it's now a venue for various exhibitions. It also hosts the access point, an information office of the municipal museums (M-Sa 09:00-13:00).

candidates.name: Orto Botanico dell'Università di Catania
candidates.content: Small botanical garden of the University of Catania.

candidates.name: Palazzo degli Elefanti
candidates.content: Construction begin in 1696. In 1736 a statue of an elephant carrying an obelisk was erected in front of the palazzo.

candidates.name: Villa Cerami
candidates.content: A Baroque villa. It hosts Faculty of Law of the University.

candidates.name: Museo Emilio Greco
candidates.content: A museum devoted to Italian artist Emilio Greco.

candidates.name: Porta Garibaldi
candidates.content: The gates erected in 1768 in honor of King Ferdinand IV and his family.

candidates.name: Federico II
candidates.alt: School of Italian language and culture
candidates.content: The school is hosted in a Baroque building downtown. The school offers year-round intensive language courses, full immersion classes for all levels, while the afternoon provides a program of cultural activities to learn the cultur

candidates.name: Via Etnea
candidates.content: Walk the main shopping avenue, running north from the Piazza del Duomo has most of the city's imposing building and is busy throughout the day and evening. Lots of churches. This road is the equivalent of Las Ramblas in Barcelona,

candidates.name: EtnaWay
candidates.content: Guided excursions on mount Etna, with transfer from Catania, Giarre or Taormina by jeep and 4x4. Visit of summit craters and most beautiful places of the volcano.

candidates.name: Grammazita
candidates.content: Bohemian bar with wine, beer, cocktails. Has live music performances most nights, LGBTQ+ friendly. Also has an associated bookshop next door with children's toys and local art prints.

candidates.name: Vermut
candidates.content: Very lively bar with a huge selection of Vermouths (as the name would imply) among other drinks. Lots of young folks in the evenings, so can be hard to find a table.

candidates.name: Retrò
candidates.content: Fancy-ish cocktail bar, with menu of original drinks inspired by famous paintings. Owners happy to talk shop about their craft.

candidates.name: L'Angolo dello Chef
candidates.content: Humble home cooking joint. Traditional Sicilian dishes from caponata to polli alla brace.

candidates.name: Sicilia in Bocca
candidates.content: Typical Sicilian food and pizza. There's another restaurant in town with this name: it's on Piazza Pietro Lupo but it's not recommended. And there's yet another 10 km north up the mountain.

candidates.name: Trattoria Il Mare
candidates.content: Delicious seafood. Casual atmosphere.

candidates.name: Camelot
candidates.content: Okay for the meat lover, fish is from frozen.

candidates.name: Il Borgo di Federico
candidates.content: A Sicilian restaurant.

candidates.name: Ristorante da Antonio
candidates.content: Italian cuisine

candidates.name: Scirocco Sicilian Fish Lab
candidates.content: Seafood

candidates.name: Dopo Teatro
candidates.content: Panineria with tables. Known for grilled meats.

candidates.name: Del centro
candidates.content: Pizza

candidates.name: Fera 'o Luni
candidates.content: A bustling food and clothes market. The main historic market of Catania.

candidates.name: La Piscaria
candidates.content: A large fish, fruit & veg market just off Piazza Duomo.
